title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures, Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines the standards, templates, operating procedures, and canonical support fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site publishing workflows, and the top support issues we encounter in customer and internal support channels. The goal is consistent, discoverable, and low-maintenance docs that reduce support load and accelerate developer on-boarding.

Scope

- SDK guides: Reference + conceptual guides for official SDKs (Go, Python, TypeScript).
- Quickstarts and templates: Minimal runnable examples, repo templates, and Postman/Insomnia collections.
- API examples: Short, copy-paste examples for common routes (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking).
- Docs site operating procedures: How to publish changes, review flows, rollback process, and CI checks.
- Top support issues & canonical fixes: Maintained list of recurring problems with step-by-step fixes.

Standards and style (required sections for every DevEx doc)

Every SDK guide / quickstart / example must include the following sections:

1) Title and 1-line summary
2) Prerequisites (SDK version, account, environment variables)
3) Quickstart (copy-paste runnable example)
4) Explanation (what each call/option means)
5) Error handling / common pitfalls
6) Links to related docs (API reference, console, release notes)
7) Ownership and test coverage (unit/integration smoke tests)

Repository structure and canonical file names

- Source repo for examples: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-examples (sync cadence: weekly)
- Template names: quickstart-<language>-<purpose>.md, sdk-guide-<language>.md, api-example-<route>.md
- Docs frontmatter: include metadata keys title, summary, sdk_version, last_tested, owner_team, doc_id

Example frontmatter (use YAML in repo files):

---
title: SDK quickstart — Python text generation
summary: Minimal Python example for text generation using Redwood API
sdk_version: 1.4.2
last_tested: 2026-11-01
owner_team: eng-developer-experience
---

SDK Guides: required content and checklist

- Supported languages: Python, TypeScript, Go. Include community SDKs as community notes.
- Each SDK guide must provide: authentication patterns, session management, streaming examples, error handling, retry/backoff recommendations, and memory/caching best practices.
- Code snippets should be runnable in <= 15 lines for the quickstart.
- Backwards compatibility policy: state minimum supported SDK version and migration notes.

Minimal Python quickstart (copy-paste)

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.text.generate(model='rw-text-1', prompt='Write a haiku about latency')
print(resp.text)
```

API Examples: canonical routes to cover

Priority examples that must exist and be kept current:

- Text generation (sync + streaming)
- Chat with system/user messages and function/tool calling
- Embeddings (batching and upsert examples)
- Reranking (score + top-k selection)
- Rate limit handling and exponential backoff

For each example include: request payload, expected response shape, pagination/batching guidance, and token/bandwidth cost estimate.

Quickstarts and Templates: distribution and maintenance

- Quickstarts should live in both the docs site and devex-examples repo. The docs site renders the canonical markdown; the repo contains runnable code and CI smoke tests.
- Templates for new examples: include test.yml (GitHub Actions) that runs a smoke test using test credentials in CI.
- Template checklist: README, LICENSE, .gitignore, run instructions, smoke-test script.

Docs site operating procedures (publish, review, rollback)

1) Drafting
- Author creates draft in the devex-examples repo or docs authoring UI. Include frontmatter with owner_team and last_tested.

2) Peer review
- At least one reviewer from eng-developer-experience must approve. Use reviewer labels: clarify feedback as 'blocking' or 'non-blocking'.

3) Automated checks (CI) — required before merge
- Linting: markdownlint and asciidoc checks
- Link-check: broken-link audit across the site
- Smoke tests: run lightweight examples against staging API keys (no production billing)
- Accessibility: image alt text and heading order check

4) Publishing
- Merge to main triggers site build and canary publish to staging docs.redwood.ai/docs-canary within 10 minutes.
- Owner receives Slack notification in #devex-docs with a link to the staging page.

5) Rollout and rollback
- Canary period: 30 minutes of manual verification for critical pages, otherwise proceed to full publish after automated checks pass.
- If a regression is reported, revert the merge via GitHub revert + new PR with fix. Follow the emergency doc fix runbook for critical customer-facing regressions.

Ownership, SLAs and operational metrics

- Doc ownership: each doc must list a single owner_team and a primary author.
- SLA for critical fixes (breaks examples or incorrect security guidance): 8 business hours to patch and merge a fix.
- SLA for non-critical content updates: 5 business days.
- Metrics to track: page views, time-to-first-byte for docs site, example-run success rate in CI, number of support tickets referencing 'docs'.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (living list)

The following are the top recurring support issues and the canonical fix steps to include in docs and internal KB. Keep this section short; link to a step-by-step internal runbook when necessary.

1) Authentication errors (401) when running examples
- Symptom: examples return 401 or 'invalid api_key'.
- Canonical fix: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and not expired; confirm env var names; run `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY` locally; if using CI, ensure secrets are configured in repo settings and masked. Owner: eng-developer-experience.

2) Streaming examples hang or cut off mid-response
- Symptom: streaming client receives partial data or stalls at token boundary.
- Canonical fix: confirm client uses streaming-aware read loops; verify network idle timeouts (NLB/GW) are >= 60s for long outputs; enable chunked transfer encoding in SDK config when using proxies. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

3) Rate limit 429 during batch embedding jobs
- Symptom: bulk embedding ingestion fails with repeated 429s.
- Canonical fix: implement exponential backoff with jitter; use server-side batching (max 512 embeddings per request recommended), and for large imports use Dedicated reserved capacity. Add a sample retry decorator in SDK guides. Owner: eng-platform.

4) Example outputs differ from production results after model upgrade
- Symptom: deterministic examples used in docs no longer match live model output.
- Canonical fix: pin model version in quickstart examples (model='rw-text-1@v2026-09-01') and add note about non-determinism; update last_tested and include small regression test in CI. Owner: applied-ml-and-evals.

5) Confusing error: 'kv-cache miss' or 'state mismatch' in multi-turn chat examples
- Symptom: chat sessions lose context or return unrelated responses.
- Canonical fix: include explicit session management sample (session_id and kv-cache header usage) and recommend setting session timeout >= 5 minutes for interactive demos. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

Canonical Fix Template (for each issue)

- Title: short description
- Symptom: bullet list of observable behaviors
- Root cause: short explanation
- Fix steps: numbered commands/steps (copy-paste where possible)
- Verification: sample request/response to confirm fix
- Owner & escalation: owner_team + escalation contact

Example: Authentication error fix steps

1) Locally: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxx`
2) Run `python examples/text_quickstart.py`
3) If 401 persists, run `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"` to inspect headers and token scope
4) If CI: verify secret is present under Settings > Secrets and that the workflow references the correct name

Maintenance and review cadence

- Owners must review their docs every 90 days and update last_tested.
- Quarterly doc audit: eng-developer-experience runs link-checks and example smoke tests across top 200 pages.
- Retire outdated examples when SDKs or APIs are EOL; mark pages with an EOL banner and link to migration guide.
